title: Aromatic Silky Saudi Arabian Lamb Tagine
description: Indulge in this rich and flavorful Saudi Arabian dish, featuring tender lamb and a blend of aromatic spices, all wrapped in a silky en-croute pastry, perfect for a special occasion, and made with buddhist-temple-friendly ingredients, avoiding any animal by-products and using garlic granules for added depth of flavor, while also incorporating a winey reduction to enhance the overall taste experience.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large bowl, whisk together garlic granules, cumin, coriander, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper.
Add the lamb pieces to the bowl and toss to coat with the spice mixture.
Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add the chopped onion to the pot and cook until browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the grated ginger to the pot and cook for 1 minute.
Add the lamb pieces to the pot and cook until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the red wine to the pot, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Bring the wine to a simmer and cook until reduced by half, about 5 minutes.
Roll out the puff pastry on a floured surface to a large rectangle, about 1/4 inch thick.
Place the lamb and onion mixture in the center of the pastry rectangle, leaving a 1 inch border around the edges.
Brush the edges of the pastry with a little water and fold the pastry over the filling, pressing the edges to seal.
Place the tagine on a baking sheet and bake for 25 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown.
